derivations.claim: If $g=0$, then $L=M=0$, so the empty determinant and $f=1$ give the formula. Suppose $g>0$. Write $L=M\oplus N$ and choose integral bases of the two rank-$g$ summands. In the combined basis, $V=\begin{pmatrix}0&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}$ with $B,C,D\in M_g(\mathbb Z)$, because $V$ vanishes on $M\times M$.

A basis change $P\in\operatorname{GL}_{2g}(\mathbb Z)$ replaces $V-tV^T$ by $P^T(V-tV^T)P$ and leaves its determinant unchanged, since $(\det P)^2=1$. Hence it suffices to calculate in the basis of step 1.1.

Put $f(t)=\det(B-tC^T)$. In $V-tV^T$ the upper-left $g\times g$ block is zero, the upper-right block is $B-tC^T$, and the lower-left block is $C-tB^T$. Swapping its two row blocks contributes $(-1)^{g^2}=(-1)^g$ and produces a block-triangular matrix, so $d_V(t)=(-1)^g\det(B-tC^T)\det(C-tB^T)$. Also $t^g f(t^{-1})=\det(tB-C^T)=(-1)^g\det(C-tB^T)$, by factoring $-1$ from each row and transposing. Therefore $d_V(t)=t^g f(t)f(t^{-1})$. The assumption on $V-V^T$ gives $d_V(1)=\pm1$, so the displayed determinant is nonzero.
Since $t^g$ is a unit in $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, the exact identity in step 3.1 implies $d_V(t)\doteq f(t)f(t^{-1})$. This proves the factorization, including the rank-zero case of step 1.1.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, oriented so that its boundary orientation is the given orientation of $K$. Let $g$ be the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of the first singular homology group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, represented by integral one-cycles on $F$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positively oriented in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. The positive push-off $a_i^+$ is the cycle carried to a sufficiently small positive normal level in a bicollar of $F$.

For disjoint oriented closed curves $J,L\subset S^3$, orient a meridian $\mu_L$ of $L$ so that a positive tangent to $L$ followed by a positive basis of its normal disk gives the ambient orientation. The linking number $\operatorname{lk}(J,L)$ is the integer determined by $[J]=\operatorname{lk}(J,L)[\mu_L]$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus L;\mathbb Z)$, using the Alexander-duality identification that sends $[\mu_L]$ to $1$. Extend linking additively over integral one-cycles. The Seifert pairing is $\theta_F(x,y)=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)$, and its matrix in the chosen basis is $V=(V_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{2g}$, where $V_{ij}=\theta_F(a_i,a_j)=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The surface and basis are part of the data; this definition asserts no knot-only matrix invariant.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is $K$, with $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ and use the positive normal convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $A_K$ be the first homology of the infinite cyclic cover of $S^3\setminus K$ classified by total linking, with $t$ acting by the positive-meridian deck transformation. Let $\Delta_K(t)$ be the generator of the zeroth elementary ideal $E_0(A_K)$ in $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, and write $p\doteq q$ when $p$ and $q$ differ by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\Lambda$. Then for every such $F$ and basis,

$$\det(V-tV^T)\doteq\Delta_K(t).$$

The determinant is $1$ for the empty $0\times0$ matrix when $g=0$. This formula concerns the polynomial $\Delta_K$; the existing knot-normalized fraction $D_K=\Delta_K/(1-t)$ is a separate invariant.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice when a knot's Seifert pairing is formed. An integral Seifert lattice is a pair $(H,V)$ in which $H$ is a free abelian group of rank $2g$ for some $g\geq0$, and $V:H\times H\to\mathbb Z$ is bilinear with $V-V^T$ unimodular. The rank-zero lattice is allowed, with the determinant of its empty skew matrix equal to $1$. A metabolizer is a primitive direct summand $M\subset H$ of rank $g$ such that $V(x,y)=0$ for every $x,y\in M$; the lattice is metabolic when it has a metabolizer. A chosen Seifert surface of an oriented knot gives such a lattice through the positive-push pairing. Its form is algebraically slice when that lattice is metabolic.

An isomorphism of integral Seifert lattices $(H,V)$ and $(H',V')$ is an integral group isomorphism $P:H\to H'$ satisfying $V'(Px,Py)=V(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in H$. Let $\mathcal S$ be the commutative monoid of these isomorphism classes under orthogonal direct sum, where $(H,V)\oplus(H',V')$ has underlying group $H\oplus H'$ and pairing $V\oplus V'$, with the rank-zero lattice as identity. The integral algebraic concordance group $G_{\mathbb Z}$ is the abelian group generated by symbols $[V]$ for $[V]\in\mathcal S$, subject to $[V\oplus W]=[V]+[W]$ and $[M]=0$ for every metabolic lattice $M$. Two selected Seifert forms are algebraically concordant when they represent the same element of $G_{\mathbb Z}$. This form relation does not assert the existence of a smooth or locally flat topological concordance annulus between the knots.

Let $g$ be a nonnegative integer, let $L$ be a free abelian group of rank $2g$, and let $V:L\times L\to\mathbb Z$ be a bilinear form whose matrix in an integral basis satisfies $\det(V-V^T)=\pm1$. Let $M\subseteq L$ be a direct summand of rank $g$ such that $V(x,y)=0$ for every $x,y\in M$. Write $d_V(t)=\det(V-tV^T)$, using the empty determinant $1$ when $g=0$. Then there is a polynomial $f(t)\in\mathbb Z[t]$ such that

$$d_V(t)=t^g f(t)f(t^{-1}).$$

In the Laurent polynomial ring, define $p\doteq q$ to mean $p=\pm t^kq$ for some integer $k$. Thus $d_V(t)\doteq f(t)f(t^{-1})$.

Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard $3$-sphere, let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $D\subset B^4$ be a locally flat properly embedded disk with oriented boundary $K$. Then the positive-push Seifert lattice $(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),V)$ is metabolic: it has a rank-$g$ primitive direct summand on which $V$ vanishes identically.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus whose core has self-linking $+1$ in the positive-push convention. Let $F$ be the genus-one Seifert surface obtained by plumbing two positive Hopf bands in a square, with oriented core curves $a,b$ forming a positive handle basis, and choose the plumbing side so that $a^+$ bounds a disk in $S^3$ disjoint from $b$. The oriented boundary of this standard positive two-band plumbing is the right-handed trefoil. In the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ with ordered basis $(a,b)$, the Seifert matrix is
$$
V=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Fix the orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ chosen for the mirror convention in the oriented connected-sum definition. If $K$ is a smooth oriented knot, its mirror $r(K)$ carries the orientation induced from $K$ by $r$. The reverse mirror of $K$, denoted $K^\dagger$, is the image $r(K)$ with its knot orientation reversed. Thus $K^\dagger$ changes both the ambient orientation convention and the orientation of the knot.

Fix a coordinate orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ for the mirror convention. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere. A connected-sum datum consists of one smoothly embedded closed three-ball around a short subarc of $K$ and one around a short subarc of $J$, each meeting its knot in a single trivial properly embedded arc, together with the fixed standard orientation-reversing boundary identification of the two standard oriented ball boundaries that joins the oriented arcs into one circle. Choose this standard map once in the standard two-ball model so that it commutes with $r$ and an orientation-preserving half-turn interchanging the two balls preserves the joining convention. Here a trivial arc is an embedded interval in a ball that is carried by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of ball-arc pairs to a straight diameter. Remove the interiors of the two balls and glue the remaining boundary spheres using this fixed identification; the resulting oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere is a connected sum of $K$ and $J$, denoted $K\#J$ for the specified datum.

The **standard unknot** is the oriented unit circle in a fixed coordinate two-plane of $S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$. A knot is **nontrivial** if it is not ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$ to the standard unknot. A nontrivial knot is **prime** if it has no connected-sum presentation whose two summand knots are both nontrivial.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For two smooth oriented knots, changing either representative by oriented ambient isotopy, changing the sufficiently small coordinate ball and trivial subarc used for either knot, or changing the positive local frame used to identify that ball with the standard oriented ball does not change the oriented ambient-isotopy class of the connected-sum knot, when the boundary gluing map is the fixed standard orientation-reversing map from the definition.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, let $B^4=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\lVert x\rVert^2\le1\}$ with boundary $S^3$. The oriented connected sum $K\#K^\dagger$ bounds a smooth properly embedded disk $D\subset B^4$ for which the squared radial function $\rho(x)=\lVert x\rVert^2$ restricts to a Morse function on the interior of $D$ with all critical points of index $0$ or $1$.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is $K$, with $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ and use the positive normal convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $A_K$ be the first homology of the infinite cyclic cover of $S^3\setminus K$ classified by total linking, with $t$ acting by the positive-meridian deck transformation. Let $\Delta_K(t)$ be the generator of the zeroth elementary ideal $E_0(A_K)$ in $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, and write $p\doteq q$ when $p$ and $q$ differ by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\Lambda$. Then for every such $F$ and basis,

$$\det(V-tV^T)\doteq\Delta_K(t).$$

The determinant is $1$ for the empty $0\times0$ matrix when $g=0$. This formula concerns the polynomial $\Delta_K$; the existing knot-normalized fraction $D_K=\Delta_K/(1-t)$ is a separate invariant.

derivations.claim: By [F1], the stated full-AC hypothesis supplies $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Apply [F5] to $T$; its conclusion gives the required smooth proper disk for $S=T\#T^\dagger$ and the stated radial critical-point indices.

Let $a_1,a_2$ be the ordered Hopf-core basis for $T$. The surface for the reverse mirror is the oppositely oriented reflected surface. Reflection reverses linking number, and the positive normal for the reverse-mirror surface is the reflected negative normal of the original. Thus its matrix entries are $-\operatorname{lk}(a_i^-,a_j)$. The identity $\operatorname{lk}(a_i^-,a_j)=\operatorname{lk}(a_j^+,a_i)$ follows by symmetry of linking and pushing the two curves to the common positive side without crossing; hence the reverse-mirror matrix is $-V^T$.

Form the boundary-connected-sum Seifert surface in the two summand balls. Cycles from different summands have zero linking because each bounds a $2$-chain in its own ball, disjoint from the other summand. The combined basis therefore has matrix $W=\operatorname{diag}(V,-V^T)$.

Let $P=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$. Direct multiplication gives $P^TV^TP=V$. The graph $M=\{(x,Px):x\in\mathbb Z^2\}$ is spanned by $e_1+e_4$ and $e_2+e_3$; projection onto the first factor identifies it with $\mathbb Z^2$, so it is a rank-$2$ direct summand. For any $x,y\in\mathbb Z^2$, $(x,Px)^TW(y,Py)=x^T(V-P^TV^TP)y=0$. Thus $M$ is a metabolizer.

The two blocks give $\det(V-tV^T)=(1-t)^2+t=t^2-t+1$ and $\det(-V^T+tV)=(t-1)^2+t=t^2-t+1$. Hence $\det(W-tW^T)=(t^2-t+1)^2$. For $f(t)=t^2-t+1$, one has $f(t^{-1})=t^{-2}f(t)$, so $\det(W-tW^T)=t^2f(t)f(t^{-1})$. By [F6], this is the claimed Fox–Milnor norm factorization of $\Delta_S$.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. A positive Hopf band is an oriented annulus whose core has self-linking $+1$ in the positive-push convention. Let $F$ be the genus-one Seifert surface obtained by plumbing two positive Hopf bands in a square, with oriented core curves $a,b$ forming a positive handle basis, and choose the plumbing side so that $a^+$ bounds a disk in $S^3$ disjoint from $b$. The oriented boundary of this standard positive two-band plumbing is the right-handed trefoil. In the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ with ordered basis $(a,b)$, the Seifert matrix is
$$
V=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is $K$, with $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ and use the positive normal convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $A_K$ be the first homology of the infinite cyclic cover of $S^3\setminus K$ classified by total linking, with $t$ acting by the positive-meridian deck transformation. Let $\Delta_K(t)$ be the generator of the zeroth elementary ideal $E_0(A_K)$ in $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, and write $p\doteq q$ when $p$ and $q$ differ by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\Lambda$. Then for every such $F$ and basis,

$$\det(V-tV^T)\doteq\Delta_K(t).$$

The determinant is $1$ for the empty $0\times0$ matrix when $g=0$. This formula concerns the polynomial $\Delta_K$; the existing knot-normalized fraction $D_K=\Delta_K/(1-t)$ is a separate invariant.

Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard $3$-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented surface with oriented boundary $K$, let $V$ be the matrix of the Seifert pairing $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ in an ordered integral basis, and let $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$. Define the **Levine–Tristram Hermitian matrix** by
$$H_\omega(V)=(1-\omega)V+(1-\bar\omega)V^T.$$
It is Hermitian because $V$ is real and $\bar\omega=\omega^{-1}$. Its signature is the number of positive eigenvalues minus the number of negative eigenvalues, both counted with multiplicity and with zero eigenvalues omitted. When $\Delta_K(\omega)\ne0$, define $\sigma_\omega(K)$ to be this signature. At a root $\omega_0\ne1$ of $\Delta_K$, define $\sigma_{\omega_0}(K)$ to be the arithmetic mean of the two one-sided limits of $\sigma_{e^{i\theta}}(K)$ as $\theta$ approaches an argument of $\omega_0$ from below and above. The invariance and one-sided-existence lemmas justify treating these values as independent of the chosen surface and basis.

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $V$ be the positive-push Seifert matrix in an ordered integral basis. Suppose the integral Seifert lattice has a rank-$g$ direct summand $M$ on which $V$ vanishes identically. For every $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$ with $\Delta_K(\omega)\ne0$, the Levine–Tristram signature $\sigma_\omega(K)$ is zero. The assertion concerns only points away from Alexander roots; no value at a root is asserted here.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $V$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix, with entries $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ in an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Let $\Delta_K(t)$ be the Alexander polynomial normalized by $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\det(V-tV^T)$, where $p\doteq q$ means $p=\pm t^kq$ for some $k\in\mathbb Z$. If the integral Seifert lattice is metabolic, then there is an $f(t)\in\mathbb Z[t]$ such that $\Delta_K(t)\doteq f(t)f(t^{-1})$. The same factorization is necessary if $K$ bounds a locally flat properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball $B^4$. This is a necessary condition for either algebraic or locally flat sliceness, not a sufficient condition. The factorization concerns the Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K$, not the separate knot-normalized fraction $D_K(t)=\Delta_K(t)/(1-t)$.

Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard $3$-sphere, let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $D\subset B^4$ be a locally flat properly embedded disk with oriented boundary $K$. Then the positive-push Seifert lattice $(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),V)$ is metabolic: it has a rank-$g$ primitive direct summand on which $V$ vanishes identically.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $\Delta_K(t)$ be its Alexander polynomial in the determinant normalization, with $p\doteq q$ meaning $p=\pm t^kq$ for some $k\in\mathbb Z$. If there is no Laurent polynomial $f(t)\in\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ such that $\Delta_K(t)\doteq f(t)f(t^{-1})$, then $K$ does not bound a locally flat properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball $B^4$. This is a necessary obstruction only; factorization alone does not assert sliceness.

derivations.claim: By [F1] and [F2], $\Delta_T(t)\doteq\det(V-tV^T)=(1-t)^2+t=t^2-t+1$. Thus $|\Delta_T(-1)|=3$, since every Laurent unit $\pm t^k$ evaluates to $\pm1$ at $-1$.

If $\Delta_T(t)\doteq f(t)f(t^{-1})$ for some $f\in\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, then evaluating at $t=-1$ gives $3=f(-1)^2$ or $-3=f(-1)^2$. Neither is possible because an integer square is nonnegative and $3$ is not an integer square. Hence the trefoil polynomial is not an integral reciprocal norm.

At $\omega=-1$, one has $H_{-1}(V)=2(V+V^T)=\begin{pmatrix}4&-2\\-2&4\end{pmatrix}$, whose eigenvalues are $2$ and $6$. Since $\Delta_T(-1)\ne0$, its Levine–Tristram signature is $2$. By [F4], a metabolic Seifert form would have signature $0$ there, so the trefoil Seifert form is not metabolic.

The polynomial and signature calculations refute algebraic sliceness. They would refute local flat sliceness through [L1] or [L2], but those supplier proofs remain unresolved in the current carriers; this item therefore remains escalated rather than claiming a completed topological refutation.
